data.gender_notes: Badrinath is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Badri means 'Berry' and Nath means 'Lord'. Badrinath is a name of Lord Vishnu, who is believed to reside in the Badrinath Temple located in the Himalayas. The name Badrinath carries the meaning “Lord Vishnu” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Badrinath usually hope their child will grow to embody lord vishnu and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes devotion and dedication to Lord Vishnu.
data.etymology: Badrinath belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord Vishnu.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Badrinath total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.cultural_impact: Badrinath is considered one of the holiest pilgrimages for Hindus. Thousands of devotees visit the shrine every year, especially during the Chardham Yatra. The place holds immense significance in Hindu mythology and culture as it is believed that visiting Badrinath bestows Moksha or salvation. The journey to Badrinath is considered pious and is often undertaken by Hindus as a part of their religious obligations.
data.spiritual_significance: Badrinath is the abode of Lord Vishnu, who is believed to reside in the form of Badrinarayan. It is said that Adi Shankaracharya discovered the idol of Badrinath in the Alaknanda River and placed it in the Temple. The presiding deity is believed to bless his devotees with intelligence, prosperity, and salvation. The temple town is rich in spiritual energy and is a place of peace and tranquility, where one can connect with God and seek spiritual growth.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Badrinath: Sanctum of Lord Vishnu, where Bhagirath performed profound penance to bring the sacred Ganges from the heavens to earth. Embodying devotion, purification and salvation.

vedic_reference.note: Badrinath is a significant Hindu pilgrimage site located in the Chamoli district, in the Indian state of Uttarakhand. The name 'Badrinath' is derived from the Sanskrit term 'Vrindavanath' which means 'Lord of Vrindavan'. Badrinath is believed to be one of the 'Panch Kedars' (Five sacred shrines) of Lord Shiva, and is considered one of the 12 Jyotirlingas.

historical_references.reference: Badrinath is believed to be the place where Lord Vishnu appeared in the form of Badarikashrama to Ved Vyas, the author of Mahabharata, and gave him the knowledge of the Mahabharata war.
historical_references.context: This reference is based on Hindu mythology and is not historically proven.

historical_references.reference: The name Badrinath is believed to have originated during the reign of the Gupta Emperor, Harshavardhana, when the Hindu religious texts mention a temple being established there.
